messages:
alex: Heads up — canary with the recent mixed-precision rollout shows a regression on endpoint `redwood-7b-rev1` when using partial per-layer quant (we exclude embeddings and lm_head). p99 increased ~12% and overall tokens/sec dropped ~20%.

maria: ouch. when did this start? which config did you flip?

alex: flipped prefer_fp8=true and enabled int8 kernels as fallback last night. Canary runs: batch=4, seq=1024 (avg prompt ~220), kv_cache enabled, sticky_kernel=false. Observed repeated kernel selection thrash and a lot of small memcpy spikes. nv/nsys profile excerpt below: 

```
# nsys summary (trimmed)
GPU Activity: 83.4%  | Memcpy: 9.2% | Other: 7.4%
kernel_selector: selected=fp8_gemm_v2 (1.4ms) -> fallback=int8_gemm_v1 (2.1ms)
kernel_launches: 1487
kvcache: evictions=312, miss_rate=0.12
small-memcpy spikes at 1.6ms between kernels
```

alex: logs show kernel_selector deciding fp8 then immediately re-evaluating for the next micro-batch and switching to int8, which causes conversion/quant-dequant work and forces some KV cache pages to be evicted due to extra allocations.

jordan: can you paste the exact kernel selector debug output? curious if it's re-evaluating due to shape/seq changes or because warmup isn't stabilizing.

alex: here, truncated: 

```
[kernel_selector] layer=attn.qkv shape=(4,220) candidates=[fp8_gemm_v2,int8_gemm_v1,fp16_gemm] scores=[0.82,0.79,0.65]
[kernel_selector] layer=attn.qkv next_batch shape=(4,512) candidates=[int8_gemm_v1,fp8_gemm_v2] scores=[0.81,0.80]
[kernel_selector] commit=fp8_gemm_v2 -> runtime.set_kernel(layer,fp8_gemm_v2)
[kernel_selector] re-eval on shape change -> picked int8_gemm_v1 -> trigger conversion path
```

maria: sequence-length variance here is large (prompt len ~220 then decode steps extend). if kernel selection is shape-sensitive we need sticky rules per-layer so we don't keep flipping while decoding.

chao: @alex this smells like two compounding issues: 1) partial quantization excludes embeddings/lm_head so calibration stats are inconsistent across KV layout (scales for intermediate layers assume full quant schedule), 2) kernel_selector doesn't have a strong hysteresis/TTL so small shape changes cause re-eval and thrash. try TTL on selection or keep kernel sticky for the duration of a request.

alex: agreed. quick experiment configs i'm going to try: 

```
# runtime config snippet
{
  "kernel_selector": {
    "sticky_per_request": true,
    "selection_ttl_ms": 5000
  },
  "quant": {
    "per_layer_overrides": ["embedding","lm_head"],
    "calibration_scope": "include_intermediates"
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "prefetch": false,
    "max_resident_pages": 1024
  }
}
```

jordan: small heads-up: turning off kv prefetch reduces latency for warmup but may increase cold misses during bursts. sticky_per_request=true should help the thrash. also add a cheap check to avoid re-eval if time_since_last_eval < 50ms.

runtime-bot: Perf regression alert: canary redwood-7b-rev1 step 2023 triggered at 1901122200. delta: p99 +12%. Linked job: ci/perf/canary-1901. See dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/canary/1901122200

chao: for the calibration side: either run a small post-quant calibration that includes a few representative decode steps (so KV statistics include decode dynamics), or allow embeddings/lm_head to keep fp16 while ensuring scales for attention are computed on mixed flows. We could also add a "calibration_mode: decode-aware" that samples across prompt+decode windows.

maria: can we repro locally with a short trace script? If someone posts a runnable docker+cmd i'll try sticky/ttl patch.

jordan: repro command (docker image with build from yesterday):

```
docker run --gpus all --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-rev1 redwood/runtime-canary:nightly \
  python perf_trace.py --batch 4 --seq 1024 --warmup 20 --iters 100 --kv=true --fp8-prefer=true
```

jordan: perf_trace will dump kernel_selector logs to /tmp/ks.log and nsys timeline to /tmp/trace.qdrep

alex: thanks. i'll run two experiments: (A) sticky_per_request + selection_ttl_ms=5s, (B) keep sticky=false but do decode-aware calibration and allow embeddings fp16. will report numbers.

chao: if A fixes it we should land a short-term patch (sticky=true) and follow up with improved calibration and a longer-term sticky-per-layer heuristic that learns stable mapping per-layer per-seq-pattern.

maria: ping me when you have numbers; i'll prep a canary rollout plan if we confirm fix. :thumbsup:

alex: starting runs now, posting results in this thread when done. thanks all.
